title: Correct policy proof HDR fact detection
summary: Correct Policy Proof Pack normalization for frame-level HDR10+ metadata and HEVC pixel-format bit depth.
reason: The mandatory HDR10+ and 10-bit catalog facts could not be verified against representative public files because the proof probe ignored frame side data and treated an empty bits_per_raw_sample field as zero depth.
behavior_before: HDR10+ present only in ffprobe frame side data normalized as HDR10, and yuv420p10le sources without bits_per_raw_sample normalized as zero-bit.
behavior_after: The bounded proof probe reads frame side data and normalizes supported high-bit-depth pixel formats when ffprobe omits the explicit raw depth.
tests_added: Policy Proof Pack captures HDR10+ from frame side data.
Policy Proof Pack infers 10-bit depth from yuv420p10le when raw depth is absent.
The ffprobe wrapper preserves the full stream inventory while requesting a separate bounded 24-frame video metadata sample.
The frame metadata probe fails closed.
Equivalent and unknown frame-rate rationals do not produce false VFR evidence.
manual_validation: RED: focused Policy Proof Pack suite ran 14 tests with six intended failures covering frame-only HDR10+, missing pixel-format depth, bounded two-probe collection, fail-closed frame probing, and equivalent/unknown frame-rate rationals.
rollback_plan: Revert the proof-normalization source and focused regressions together; no production media policy, source media, or package runtime state is changed.
notes:
Discovered with the repository's previously approved public Dolby Browser Test Kit and FFPictures HDR10+ validation sources. This change does not alter FFmpeg command generation or publish policy.
Add RED regressions for frame HDR10+ and pixel-format bit-depth normalization.
Refresh the canonical test summary after adding RED regressions.
